13287.name: Jeremiyah Love

brief.prose: Arizona's lead back when healthy, a rookie first-round pick, and on injured reserve with a right high-ankle sprain projected at four to five weeks, so Week 13 is the earliest he can return. Mike LaFleur had said Bam Knight was planned as a top-two back before both were hurt in Week 8, but Knight is now ruled out at Seattle with the concussion, leaving Tyler Allgeier to lead a depleted group. The cap is a month for other backs to establish themselves; the watch is whether Knight's protocol clears for Week 10 and whether the ankle holds on Love's return.
brief.rationale: IR with a 4-to-5 week projection overstates any season projection on his workload; Allgeier is the only healthy lead back this week.

13294.name: Makai Lemon

brief.prose: A first-round rookie drafted to help replace A.J. Brown (traded to New England), but the path to early snaps is murkier than the pedigree suggests. A hamstring cost him two weeks; he returned limited on Aug. 20 and is racing to catch up on the install before Week 1. Beyond DeVonta Smith (the focal point), Philadelphia also added veterans Hollywood Brown, Elijah Moore and Dontayvion Wicks, so the WR2 job is crowded. The half-PPR upside is real long-term, but the injury and veteran competition make him a stash/late dart in redraft, not an immediate contributor.
brief.rationale: High-pedigree rookie back from a hamstring but behind on the install and buried in a veteran-added room; a redraft stash, not a Week 1 contributor.

Washington then signed Stefon Diggs on a one-year deal, and camp reporting since has Williams sliding into a slot role behind McLaurin and Diggs rather than fighting for outside WR2 snaps, a role beat writers frame as favorable for a rookie's development but is a clear target-competition downgrade from where he stood two weeks earlier. This is a real, recent role delta that may not be fully reflected yet.
brief.rationale: Diggs' Aug 5 signing bumped Williams from presumptive outside WR2 to slot depth behind two veterans; off the draftable board, a dynasty/waiver watch rather than a draft consideration.

brief.prose: Kubiak's offense, which spread touches across a deep Seahawks backfield, is giving the rookie fourth-rounder real first- and second-team reps behind lead back Ashton Jeanty, not just camp-body work. Kubiak said he 'has grown a lot since OTAs,' and Jeanty said there's 'no drop-down' when Washington is in. That's standard complementary positioning for a Day 3 rookie behind an entrenched starter, consistent with a late ADP. He's the Jeanty handcuff with a little standalone juice, but in a 5-bench league that's a stash worth taking only if you drafted Jeanty and can spare the spot.
brief.rationale: Complementary rookie behind Jeanty; a Jeanty-handcuff stash that 5 bench spots make a luxury unless you own the lead back.
